issue.title: Bug: auto-mode safety review request drops reasoning_content, DeepSeek rejects it and the action is held

expected: In default auto permission mode, a DeepSeek thinking-mode safety review should preserve the required reasoning metadata and return a valid review decision, rather than fail because the request omits reasoning_content.
defect: The safety-review request lacks reasoning_content. In two of ten fixed-case archived executions, DeepSeek rejects it and fx holds a requested shell action with review_unavailable.

fault location.explanation: The pending assistant is copied but provider_replay is explicitly set to null before constructing the review messages, dropping provider-specific reasoning metadata.
The review messages are expanded and serialized through the chat-completions provider; this path does not restore the reasoning replay removed during review composition.

Root cause: At the reported tested commit, the auto-review composer copies the pending assistant tool call but sets provider_replay=null, removing the provider-specific reasoning metadata before build_review serializes the request. DeepSeek thinking mode sometimes rejects the missing reasoning_content; fx then holds the action because review is unavailable. The archived environment used fx acp, default auto permissions and a custom openai-chat-completions connection to DeepSeek/deepseek-v4-flash. The ten retained runs use h2-v1 unchanged, including misses: network logs for run-01 and run-03 contain the reasoning_content rejection, matching the archived 2/10 result. This did not meet the original 7/10 GT threshold. The source explains the omission, but why the provider accepts some otherwise affected requests is unresolved. No new model execution or fix regression test was performed. fixed_in is unknown; pinned_contains_fix=false refers to the inspected historical code.
